title: Hippocampal sequences represent working memory and implicit timing
goal: Reproduce the source's central empirical findings on unexpected-delay working-memory behavior and odor-selective CA1 sequences, including the original time- and odor-encoding comparisons, using each analysis's complete source-defined cohort and indispensable controls. Assess Fig. 4D time-decoder improvement as a separately named result-level method outcome on the original observations and evaluation. Improved decoding alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement of the biological findings.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: The retained empirical family comprises unexpected-delay working-memory accuracy and lick latency (Figure 1C-D), cue-specific CA1 sequences and their validation (Figure 2D-F and relevant S1 controls), baseline-versus-current activity information and time decoding (Figure 4A-D), and original odor-identity decoding companions (S6). Preserve the distinct 23-mouse behavior and 11-mouse imaging cohorts, source trial/session identities and indispensable controls; no every-figure, raw-movie reprocessing or unrelated trajectory/PCA requirement is inferred.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: The Figure 4C-D real/shuffled time decoder is a genuine empirical decoding/modeling result, not simulation or preprocessing. Retain the complete seven-bin short/long source comparison, standard-cue trial masks, leave-one-trial-out evaluation, correlations and confusion matrices. Figure 4D improvement is a separately named partial result; it cannot satisfy complete primary behavior/sequence/information reproduction or improvement, so the mixed-target primary-reproduction/partial-decoder-improvement bundle remains unavailable.
